assessment_summary: The statement is Tutte's bipartite conjecture, which claims that every 3-connected cubic bipartite graph is Hamiltonian. This is a known false statement. The first discovered counterexample is the Horton graph on 92 vertices, and the minimal counterexamples (proven to be the smallest possible) are the Georges and Kelmans graphs on 50 vertices.
counterexample: The Horton graph (92 vertices). Explicit small structure: It is constructed from 4 copies of a 23-vertex bipartite gadget (two copies with 3 black terminals, two copies with 3 white terminals) connected by a perfect matching between their terminals. Explicit trace: Any Hamiltonian cycle in the full 92-vertex graph must enter and leave at least one of these 23-vertex gadgets exactly once, which would induce a Hamiltonian path between two of its terminals. However, the 23-vertex gadget is explicitly designed to have no Hamiltonian path between any pair of its terminals, thus no Hamiltonian cycle can exist.
